verdicts.note: IVF/ICSI twin pregnancy risks and prevention.
Danish epidemiology of infertility and assisted reproduction. Denmark is arm 1's best-covered register population (Sobotka 2008).
Labour supply after health shocks. Reached by citation path only.
Postponing versus rejecting parenthood among female academics — the distinction matters for P6, since only postponers are candidates for ART repair.
Parental well-being and parity progression.
Cardiovascular risk in infertile men.

Population Studies 2024: CHANGE OVER TIME in the perceived reproductive age window, against delayed fertility in Europe. A moving belief measured against a moving behaviour across countries — the strongest observational design in P6 so far.
Natural conception rates across Danish cohorts. B's.
**'HOW IMPORTANT IS SELECTION?' on ART and IUI delivery outcomes.** Selection into treatment is what decides whether an ART birth is additional; this asks the question arm 1 usually assumes away.
Nepal; tag SECONDARY under Wall 8.
Review of the social-psychological experience of infertility.
Human Reproduction Update review of the demographic and medical consequences of postponement — the standard synthesis P4's estimates sit inside, and one of the most-cited records in the frame.
Age changes in cycle fecundability, separating coital frequency from ageing. A.14's input.
Dissertation on postponement and low fertility in Europe.
No abstract. Cumulative conception and live-birth rates after IVF, Lancet 1992.
No abstract. Lancet piece on preservation for age-related decline — elective indication named in the title.
Melatonin and ovarian ageing in MICE.
US infertility service use, 1995 — a pre-mandate-era utilisation baseline.

A new estimate of permanent sterility by age. Another P4 parameter, and note the qualifier in its own abstract: 'unless medical assistance is used' — the models know ART sits outside their sterility curve.
No abstract. US infertility evaluation and treatment prevalence.
Edited volume on childbearing trends in low-fertility countries.
Global burden of PCOS-attributable infertility. B.4's.
No abstract. Coverage and IVF outcomes, US.
Italian students' knowledge of ART LEGISLATION as well as fertility — legal availability entering the belief channel.
Is human fecundity declining? B.2/B.6's question.
Medicinal plants and ovarian function.
'How old is too old?' — AGE LIMITS on ART access. Second record on P2's legal-eligibility margin alongside the comparative regulation study in batch 5.

JPAM review of US NATALIST POLICIES, deliberate and incidental. Places ART mandates among the other levers, which is what the demographic-significance stage needs in order to say whether this one matters relative to the rest.
IFFS Surveillance 2013 — the global survey of ART regulation, funding and availability. The cross-national access variation P2 would need, in one document.
Saudi Arabia; tag SECONDARY under Wall 8.
Parenting adjustment after assisted versus spontaneous conception.

Telemedicine parity laws and mortality. Reached because it shares the state-insurance-mandate design, not the topic — a good illustration of why the frame is drawn on citations rather than vocabulary.
A birth-register data resource for MALE fertility. Peripheral to A.17 but relevant to A.16.
Time-to-pregnancy measurement in the Polish GGS.
Stigma toward involuntarily childless women.
No abstract. Canadian fertility decline since the Great Recession.
Infertility prevalence in Iran. Wall 4.
Clinical management of fertility over 40. Note the abstract's own claim that women OVERESTIMATE the age of decline — P6's mechanism asserted inside a clinical text.
'Can we expand the women's reproductive lifespan?' — elective cryopreservation against involuntary childlessness. Second P5 record posing a fertility outcome rather than an attitude.
Implicit attitudes toward childfree women.
Sulfa drugs and mortality decline. A methodological cousin — a medical-technology diffusion shock — reached by citation, not topic.
ESHRE European IVF Monitoring, 2015 edition. The series the anchor set holds at 2014.
Tobacco exposure and fecundity. B.4's.
Hong Kong students, compared with Western samples.
Psychometric validation of an attitudes scale.
Dutch dissertation on remaining childless.
High fertility of secular Israeli Jews. NOTE for the Israel records: Israel's unusual fertility level is the context in which its free-IVF policy operates, which bears on transportability.
ART cost to an HMO.
Systematic review of student fertility awareness. Second SR of this cell — the belief side is now reviewed twice over while the behaviour side has no primary studies.
Preservation coverage for surgical trainees.
Qualitative study of childless Black women and compulsory mothering.

**Decomposes MAR multiple births by PROCEDURE TYPE — first-line ovarian stimulation versus IVF — and over time. A.12 needs this: it separates the ovulation-induction channel single-embryo-transfer policy does not touch.** Route with a strong flag.

**EIGHT-YEAR FOLLOW-UP of 892 women and 193 men after fertility assessment and counselling, with FAMILY FORMATION as the outcome.** The first record in P6 that follows a belief intervention through to actual childbearing. If the P6 cell has a behaviour-side study at all, this is it. Priority full-text.
Nigerian students; tag SECONDARY under Wall 8.
Qualitative: social egg freezing and the dating market. Names the partnership channel — egg freezing as a response to not having a partner, which is A.24's and C.7's territory meeting A.17's.
Review of elective preservation effectiveness, safety and law.
Survey-module design for first reproductive experience.
Over-the-counter switches for emergency contraception. A.2/A.4's, and well identified — same policy-shock family, opposite direction.

Italy: NO socio-economic differences in ART treatment SUCCESS, against documented disparities in ART births. If success is equal but births are not, the disparity is in access rather than in response — which is arm 2's premise stated as a finding.
Lutz et al. on European negative momentum.
